Trading activity in Nigeria’s official foreign exchange market suffered a sharp contraction on Tuesday, with interbank turnover plunging by 82.36 per cent to $164.28 million, down from $931.23 million recorded in the previous session. The $766.95m decline in daily transactions represents one of the sharpest contractions in recent trading activity, reversing the surge in foreign exchange turnover recorded in the preceding sessions. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria’s FX trading activities showed that the value of transactions fell by nearly five-sixths within 24 hours, while the number of deals also declined significantly. The number of transactions dropped by 39.46 per cent to 135 on Tuesday from 223 recorded on Monday, indicating a substantial reduction in the volume and frequency of trading among market participants. The latest turnover was also 79.85 per cent lower than the $815.57m recorded on Friday, while the number of deals fell by 24.58 per cent from 179 transactions recorded on the same day. Monday’s $931.23m turnover had represented the highest level in one month, making Tuesday’s sharp reversal particularly significant. The sudden decline raises questions about the consistency of liquidity and participation in the official foreign exchange market, especially as businesses and investors continue to navigate exchange rate uncertainty. Although the data do not establish whether the decline resulted from reduced dollar supply, weaker demand or lower participation by market operators, the scale of the contraction highlights the volatility of trading activity in the market. Naira weakens to N1,455/$ as reserves shed $108m CBN holds rate at 23%, warns of election spending T-bill yield climbs to 17.82% on sell-off The reduction in turnover also coincided with further weakness in the naira, which closed at N1,397/$ per dollar on Wednesday in the official market, compared with N1,393 on Monday. The currency traded between N1,389 and N1,398 during the session, while the simple average exchange rate stood at N1,394.31 per dollar. The latest closing rate was the weakest in nearly nine months, while the parallel market exchange rate stood at N1,445 per dollar. The decline in interbank turnover comes amid persistent FX market pressure, with the naira losing N50.49, or 3.75 per cent, against the dollar between 2 November and 24 November. The Central Bank of Nigeria retained its benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent at its latest Monetary Policy Committee meeting, as policymakers continued to monitor inflationary and exchange rate pressures. The apex bank has also recently authorised commercial banks to sell up to $1m in physical cash to Bureau De Change operators, in a move aimed at increasing dollar availability in the retail FX market. However, the impact of the intervention on overall market liquidity and exchange rate stability remains to be seen. Further trading data will be important in determining whether Tuesday’s collapse in turnover was an isolated disruption or signals a sustained decline in activity in Nigeria’s interbank foreign exchange market. Odinaka Anudu
